Alex — thanks for the template and the clear asks. I put together a concise runbook and attached a dedicated_canary_runbook.pdf plus a short sizing checklist. High level proposal below; see attachments for the detailed scripts and exact metrics we’ll collect.

Summary plan (proposal):
1) Pre-acceptance (1 week) — Rightsize validation in staging
   - We will replay 72 hours of representative traffic from your CSV against a dedicated staging pool sized to your 99th percentile peak concurrency.
   - Success gates: 95th/99th token latency within 15% of Hosted baseline and no >0.5% error-rate increase.
2) Canary (2 days) — Nightly 10% traffic split for 2 consecutive evenings (22:00–02:00 PT)
   - Monitored signals: per-request latency, top-token-diff rate (quality drift), token cost delta, OOMs, CPU/GPU memory pressure.
   - Automatic abort if quality drift >2% on key prompt set or latency regression >40% vs baseline.
3) Ramp & acceptance (1 week) — daily increments: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%
   - Run a verification suite at each step (synthetic and customer-sampled prompts).
4) Cutover window & rollback plan — we recommend a weekend low-traffic window (Sat 02:00–06:00 PT) if full swap is required.
   - Immediate fallback: route traffic back to Hosted API for routes with >5% error surge or if any data-plane SLA breach detected.
5) Post-cutover monitoring (30 days) — extra retention of logs and daily sanity checks by on-call.

Operational notes:
- Model config: we recommend starting with fp16 + guided per-route quantization only if the acceptance suite shows no quality regression.
- Autoscaling: set upper bound to 1.5x projected peak for first 72h; we’ll tune based on observed cold-start profile.
- Billing: switch billing to Dedicated metering at 100% cutover; we can provide a short grace-credit if runbook failures cause a rollback during the first week.

Next steps I need from your side (by EOD Thu):
- Confirm the slice of prompts you want used for the quality check (shortlist attached or point to a Drive folder).
- Approve the night-time canary windows and the safety abort thresholds above.

I’ll loop Marcus for the technical acceptance automation and Laura for SLA/ops coordination.

—
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success (onramp)
Redwood Inference
